contestNote: The mandatory 0.25% GDP Ukraine military pledge was NOT adopted at Helsingborg. Rutte confirmed on Day 2 (May 22) that the proposal will not advance in its current mandatory form — France, the UK, and several western European allies opposed the rigid formula, fearing budget strain and entrenchment of the conflict. Ukrainian FM Sybiha, present at both Day 1's Sofiero Palace dinner and Day 2's plenary, pressed for a binding commitment but consensus could not be formed. The pledge will be repackaged as softer, non-binding language ahead of the Ankara Leaders' Summit (July 7–8, 2026). Total allied Ukraine support via PURL remains ~$47-48B/year; Rutte's original proposal would have raised this to ~$143B/year. Eastern allies (Poland, Baltics) supported the pledge; France and UK rejected it. Outcome: deferral.
